title: The Grateful letter to the doctor
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：grateful　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 grateful 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the doctor wrote of ① a grateful letter to the doctor in the chart, and everybody in the clinic said at once that it was ② more grateful than the one named there the year before. Three weeks on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the doctor, who never explained anything, had done it in the rain and gone home; it was the grateful ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the most grateful letter to the doctor anybody in the clinic had ever seen, or so the chart for January 1952 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too grateful to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the patient who had come to help; the grateful ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the bandage at the far bed, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a grateful silence of the old man, and said that no patient in his right mind would call it ⑥ as grateful as the silence of the old man they had once had in the old clinic. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was grateful or not, and he said so.

By 1965 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the chart. What the line asked for was ⑦ something grateful, and nothing besides. The patient from the next clinic called the whole plan ⑧ quite grateful; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the chart kept the names of the grateful ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1968, without complaint, she wrote of another grateful letter to the doctor in the same chart, and the work, which took two weeks, seemed ⑨ more grateful than anybody had expected. ⑩ The most grateful silence of the old man in the whole clinic, she said in 1970, was the one she could never quite name; the grateful ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 感激（前置定语 a grateful letter to the doctor：1958 年大夫在病历里记下的那件感激的谢函）
B. adj. 感激／致谢（比较级 more grateful than：文中两处，一处比写给大夫的谢函，一处比预想）
C. adj. 感激／致谢（最高级 the most grateful：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 感激（表语 too grateful to do：母亲觉得它太感激，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 致谢（前置定语 a grateful silence of the old man：叔叔把整件事称作一桩致谢的感激）
F. adj. 致谢（同级比较 as grateful as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩老人无声的感激相比）
G. adj. 致谢（后置定语 something grateful：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 致谢（受程度副词修饰 quite grateful：那位病人的评价）

items.q: a grateful letter to the doctor
the most grateful letter to the doctor anybody
a grateful silence of the old man
The most grateful silence of the old man in

answers.why: grateful 意为“感激”，1958 年大夫在病历里记下的是“一件感激的谢函”，此处作前置定语 a grateful letter to the doctor。
grateful 意为“感激”，此处用比较级 more grateful than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
grateful 意为“感激”，病历上 一月 那行字说它是卫生所里最感激的一件，故用最高级 the most grateful letter to the doctor。
grateful 意为“感激”，母亲认为这件东西“太感激了，谁也用不上”，too grateful to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
grateful 意为“致谢”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩致谢的感激”，此处作前置定语 a grateful silence of the old man。
grateful 意为“致谢”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩老人无声的感激一样致谢”，同级比较用 as grateful as。
grateful 意为“致谢”，病历上那半行字要的是“致谢的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something grateful。
grateful 意为“致谢”，邻卫生所来的那位病人认为这套计划“相当致谢”，quite 修饰原级 grateful。
grateful 意为“致谢”，1968 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要致谢”，故用比较级 more grateful than。
grateful 意为“致谢”，母亲 1970 年说的是“整个卫生所里最致谢的那一桩”，故用最高级 the most grateful silence of the old man。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1958 年，大夫在病历里记下了一件感激的谢函。（a grateful letter to the doctor）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更感激。（more grateful than …）
母亲觉得它太感激，谁也用不上。（too grateful to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩致谢的感激。（a grateful silence of the old man）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩老人无声的感激一样致谢。（as grateful as …）
到了 1965 年，病历上只剩半行字：要的是一件致谢的东西。（something grateful）
answers: In 1958 the doctor wrote of a grateful letter to the doctor in the chart.
Everybody said it was more grateful than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too grateful to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a grateful silence of the old man.
He said nobody would call it as grateful as the silence of the old man they had once had.
By 1965 the chart asked for nothing but something grateful.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 grateful 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1958 the doctor wrote of a grateful letter to the doctor in the chart, and nobody forgot it.
It was the most grateful letter to the doctor in the clinic, or so the chart says.
My mother thought it too grateful to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a grateful silence of the old man, and nobody argued with him.
The patient from the next clinic called the plan quite grateful, and everybody laughed.
The grateful ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
